title: Pooled Shotgun Metagenomics Reveals Cloacal Microbiota Composition and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in Chickens from Kazakhstan
content: Monitoring the poultry microbiota and antimicrobial resistance genes is important, as they can reflect flock health, farm conditions and the level of antimicrobial resistance. However, data from shotgun metagenomics describing the profiles of the cloacal microbiota and resistome of poultry in Kazakhstan are limited. In this study, taxonomic and antimicrobial resistance profiles were characterized in pooled metagenomes of the cloacal microbiota of chickens sampled from backyard and commercial poultry farms in Kazakhstan. Cloacal swabs were collected from laying hens, pooled at the house level, and analyzed using high-throughput metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic profiles were generated at the genus level, while antimicrobial resistance gene signals were summarized by drug class. Compositional patterns were assessed using CLR/Aitchison ordination, the Mantel test, and Procrustes analysis. The pooled samples exhibited heterogeneous microbiota profiles at the genus level and included taxa of veterinary interest, such as Chlamydia, Avibacterium, and Gallibacterium. Resistome profiling revealed a broad but unevenly distributed set of antimicrobial resistance signals, including classes associated with tetracyclines, fluoro-quinolones, aminoglycosides, and beta-lactams. Taxonomic and resistome profiles showed preliminary alignment at the matrix level, indicating that resistome variations are partially linked to microbial community structure.
